members.name: player_id
members.notes: Logged as 'MAKECHR[pid]'. Used as the join key for CMD_RENAME's list walk: each existing slot entry whose first dword equals this gets the new name + doRename flag patched in place.

members.name: character_id
members.notes: Logged as 'MAKECHR[cid]'.

members.name: slot_or_chrindex
members.notes: Character slot index, read as a single byte by FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024): `*(byte *)(body + 0x18)` on the CMD_MAKE path, bounds-checked against the local slot count and then passed to the 0x2E0-stride slot indexer FUN_006B3D40 (BCS-Y-0096). Logged through the byte-value numeric ostream overload FUN_005434A0 (BCS-Y-1823), not the const char* overload, so the u8 width is parser-confirmed. The server and the parity baseline both write a u32 type constant 0x400017 across body+0x18..0x1B; little-endian that puts 0x17 (23) in the byte this parser reads, which exceeds any real slot count, so CMD_MAKE always takes the 'INVALID CHRINDEX 23 for MAKECHR' log branch and falls through to the append path rather than the in-place REPLACE path. That is the correct outcome for a newly created character, which is why the live client accepts the packet. The remaining three bytes of the server's constant are unread by this parser (see unknown_1A).

members.name: do_rename
members.notes: Per-entry needs-rename flag. CMD_RENAME copies this byte into the existing matched character entry at entry+9.

members.name: unknown_1A
members.notes: Not read by the decoded handlers.

members.name: ticket
members.notes: Logged as 'MAKECHR[tkt]'.

members.name: name
members.notes: Character name. Logged as 'MAKECHR[nam]'. Copied into the existing matched character entry at entry+4 on CMD_RENAME.

members.name: world_name
members.notes: World name, NUL-terminated ASCII. FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024) logs it as 'MAKECHR[wld]' by passing the ADDRESS body+0x40 to the const char* ostream overload FUN_004E7290 (BCS-Y-1821), in the identical two-call shape it uses for the character name at body+0x20; the pid / cid / ticket fields at body+0x10 / +0x14 / +0x1C instead load their value and pass it to the numeric overload FUN_00DA9670 (BCS-Y-1822). The overload split is the parser-side proof that body+0x40 is a string, not a scalar. Supersedes the earlier `world_id` uint32_t reading, which was a decode error, not a server error: the server writes a 32-byte padded ASCII world name here (kLobbyCharaCreatorWorldNameSize = 0x20), matching the parity baseline, and the live 1.23b client accepts it. Width 0x20 is taken from the server / parity-baseline field size; the parser itself only requires NUL termination.

members.name: remainder
members.notes: Remaining 368 bytes of the response body. The handler does not read fields past body+0x40 by name; instead bytes from body+0x10 through at least body+0x1E0 are copied into a local 0x2E0-byte buffer (with the trailing 0x110 bytes zeroed) and pushed onto a slot vector via FUN_00891F00. The handler thus implicitly assumes the body extends at least to body+0x1E0 (480 bytes), 16 bytes past the explicitly-named region; see BCS-S-0009 SlotEntry for the slot's interpretation and MDI-014 for the open width question.

types.notes: s2c body for lobby opcode 0x0E (CharacterModify response). The handler (FUN_00DA79D0 / BCS-Y-0024) explicitly reads fields out to body+0x60 (world_name), but the body must extend to at least body+0x1E0 (480 bytes) because the push path copies 0x1D0 bytes starting at body+0x10. Documented size 0x1D0 reflects the named-field region; the actual on-the-wire body size remains open and is annotated on the remainder field. Re-anchored against the client parser (see phase-ledger the lobby-0x0e-0x0d-parser-re-anchor pass): the named region now agrees field-for-field with the server / parity-baseline layout (u64 sequence, u8 1, u8 1, u16 command @0x0A, u32 0, u32 pid @0x10, u32 cid @0x14, u32 type constant 0x400017 @0x18, u32 ticket @0x1C, 0x20-byte ASCII name @0x20, 0x20-byte ASCII world name @0x40). Two prior divergences resolved: body+0x40 was catalogued as a u32 `world_id` and is in fact an ASCII string (the parser hands its address to the const char* ostream overload); body+0x18 is genuinely read as a u8 by the client even though the server writes a u32 there, and the resulting 'INVALID CHRINDEX 23' branch is the normal append path for a new character. Shares the chara-list per-character record (BCS-S-0008) stride and feeds the same slot-entry vector (this+0x1D4..this+0x1D8, element stride 0x2E0) via the push path FUN_00891F00 (BCS-Y-0023 = std::vector::push_back). The two layouts are the SAME field frame offset by 0x10: this body's name at body+0x20 lands at slot entry+0x10, which is exactly where BCS-S-0008's record+0x20 name lands (see BCS-S-0008 notes for the three-way frame proof). The push does not source the body directly: the handler builds a local 0x2E0-byte buffer (body+0x10..body+0x1E0 copied to local[0..0x1D0), local[0x1D0..0x2D0) zeroed) and pushes that local. See BCS-S-0009 for the resulting slot layout. Earlier notes incorrectly described FUN_00891F00 as a 're-parser' (it is push_back) and as receiving body directly (it receives the local buffer). The packet is shared across the five sub-commands: the server emits this response after RESERVE/MAKE/RENAME/DELETE/RENAME_RETAINER to deliver the post-operation character state. Distinct from BCS-S-0007 CharacterModifyRequest which the client sends on the c2s side: same opcode, different layout, different command field offset and width (see MDI-024).

It cannot classify type-0x000D fields invariant or dynamic across sessions because the other session has no such opcode. Unnamed spans remain opaque; former server-lineage field names were removed because this client route does not consume them.

Per client-architecture '1.x combat is asymmetric' (1.x combat asymmetry), inventory operations ride the generic event-family frame (0x012D EventStart + 0x012E EventUpdate) rather than using a dedicated inventory opcode. **Field relabeling**: offset 0x00..0x10 fields retain the pcap-derived labels with the original opcode-payload-schemas labels preserved as `_or_` suffixes. symbols.name: CharaListParser_FUN_00DA76B0
symbols.notes: Direct s2c opcode-0x000D parser reached only from BCS-Y-0017 with packet+0x10. It clears the slot vector when body+0x08 bits 1..7 are zero, loops over the u8 count at body+0x09 with 0x1D0 record-window stride, and looks up each record+0x18 low-six-bit key in the 0x2E0-stride vector at this+0x1D0. Existing keys append the unbounded NUL-terminated record+0x50 string to the first NUL at slot+0x40. New keys copy record+0x10 for 0x1D0 bytes, zero 0x100 bytes, initialize an empty embedded vector, and push through BCS-Y-0023; upper key bits request a 0x3F mask over every destination key byte. The parser returns the inverse of control-flags bit 0. It has vector-state checks through FUN_009D22B4 but no payload-length, count-to-length, string-scan, or append-capacity validation. symbols.name: s2c_payload_byte_diff_receiver_struct_extraction
symbols.notes:
**the inbound-payload-schemas pass: s2c receiver payload byte-diff schemas**. Mirror of the opcode-payload-schemas pass on the s2c side. The lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass wire-confirmation pass identified 16 of 38 inbound receivers as observed in the 54-scenario pcap corpus; this manifest extracts the empirical payload layout for the 7 with the heaviest sample counts.

**Method**: extended the opcode-payload-schemas pass's pcap parser with the direction filter inverted (s2c streams = server -> client per private-IP heuristic). zlib-decompress is_compressed=1 BasePacket bodies (s2c is typically compressed); SubPacket + GameMessage framing is direction-agnostic. For each target opcode collect every emission's post-GameMessage-header inner bytes, group by length; all 7 yielded fixed-length payloads (no variable-size opcodes in this set). Per-byte entropy bucketing surfaces invariant zero padding runs, invariant non-zero constants, and the active varying-data regions.

**Sample counts and shapes**: 0x0137 SyncMemoryReceiver 79 samples / 136-byte body (94-byte sync state + 42-byte zero pad), 0x0136 SetEventStatusReceiver 43 / 40 (1-byte status + 3-pad + 15-byte event metadata + 18-pad + 3-byte trailing data), 0x0144 ChangeActorSubStatModeBorderReceiver 36 / 8 (compact mode + border block), 0x0145 ChangeActorExtraStatReceiver 30 / 8 (1-byte stat-kind + 7-byte zero pad), 0x0179 ChangeActorSubStatStatusReceiver 30 / 40 (ENTIRELY-ZERO 40-byte body), 0x017b ChangeShadowActorFlagReceiver 30 / 8 (ENTIRELY-ZERO 8-byte body), 0x013d SetDisplayNameReceiver 30 / 40 (3-byte name-table selector + 37-byte zero pad).

**Key empirical finding**: 0x0179 and 0x017b have **entirely zero bodies across all 30 samples each** - the delta these receivers apply is conveyed via the GameMessage HEADER (the opcode itself selects which sub-stat changes, the src field carries the actor ID being updated), and the body is reserved/empty. This is a previously-unrecognized 1.x receiver pattern: 'header-only delta'. Multiple Change* receivers in the 0x0144..0x017b range share this shape; the body size varies (8 or 40 bytes) but is always all-zero. The body sizes are likely a compile-time default tied to the receiver class hierarchy, not used as actual payload space.

**Promoted to BCS-S**: 7 new struct entries BCS-S-0019..0025 in namespace FFXIV.Client.Network.Wire.S2C, each named after its receiver class: SyncMemoryReceiverPayload, SetEventStatusReceiverPayload, ChangeActorSubStatModeBorderReceiverPayload, ChangeActorExtraStatReceiverPayload, ChangeActorSubStatStatusReceiverPayload, ChangeShadowActorFlagReceiverPayload, SetDisplayNameReceiverPayload. All confidence 'confirmed-pcap-derived'. Field sizes sum exactly to each opcode's innerLen.

**Combined coverage with the opcode-payload-schemas pass**: 13 BCS-S wire-struct entries now exist across c2s (0013..0018) and s2c (0019..0025) - the receiver-side wire layout is now anchored for the 7 heaviest inbound opcodes covering combat-receive (party_battle_leve), zone-transition (gridania_to_coerthas), and movement scenarios. Tooling: tools/extractors/extract_inbound_payload_schema.py + summarize_schemas.py + synthesize_field_layouts.py + append_struct_entries.py. Outputs: manifests/inbound_payload_schemas.json + manifests/inbound_proposed_field_layouts.json + 7 new BCS-S entries.

Paired each wire struct (BCS-S-0019..0025) with its Receive() apply method to surface actor-state field writes and validate the inbound-payload-schemas pass 'header-only delta' hypothesis. **Method**; per project-receiver-vtable-layouts memory; 6 of the 7 receivers are 2-slot (Receive at slot 1 = slot1Fn; receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json); ChangeActorSubStatStatus (0x0179) is 5-slot (slot 1 is the New() factory; real Receive at slot 2 = FUN_008A3550 Decomped all 7 Receive entries and the 8 direct helpers + FUN_006EEC00 (the CharaBase+0xDC sub-struct lazy initializer used by 0x0144/0x0145/0x0179). **Pattern split**: the 7 receivers fall into 3 apply patterns. (1) **Direct CharaBase sub-struct writers**: 0x013D SetDisplayName writes CharaBase+0x60->[0,0x58,0x59] (display name id + kind + is-unset flag) and FIRES `_onUpdateDisplayName` Lua callback via FUN_006FAFF0 (NEW Lua-firer evidence - this name was previously excluded from the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass bridge as a false positive; the receiver-apply-findings pass evidence places it CORRECTLY at depth 2 of the 0x013D apply chain). 0x0144 ChangeActorSubStatModeBorder writes CharaBase+0xDC->[0x18] (mode-border byte via FUN_006EECB0). 0x0145 ChangeActorExtraStat writes CharaBase+0xDC->[0x10] (net-stat u32) via FUN_006FA980 and bit-fires `_onChangeNetStatUser` (bits 8..15) and `_onChangeNetStatSystem` (bits 0x10/0x11/0x12) for changed bits (NEW Lua-firer evidence; 2 NEW direct binding candidates for the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass bridge). (2) **Indirect via vtable / lookup**: 0x0136 SetEventStatus (target NpcBase) does a switch on receiver+0x58 status-kind byte and dispatches to vtable[9] of a looked-up state object; 0x0137 SyncMemory maintains a separate sync-memory cache via FUN_00775A30; 0x0179 routes through 5-slot slot-3 dispatcher FUN_008A3630 -> FUN_007084B0 -> FUN_006EEC00 + FUN_00707D60 (actual write at depth 4 not decomped). (3) **Direct field write to known offset**: 0x017B ChangeShadowActorFlag writes target+0x5d via FUN_006DBE50 (already in data_dependency_catalog from BCS-Y-0278). **Header-only-delta hypothesis CONFIRMED for 0x0179 and 0x017B**. For 0x0179: wire body is all-zero (40 bytes); the apply works by (a) RTTI-casting a secondary-actor pointer to StatusBase and caching it at receiver+0x10, (b) reading receiver+0x14 sub-stat-enum byte (which IS zero because wire is all-zero), (c) calling FUN_007084B0(target, 0, cachedPrimary, 1) - so the meaningful delta info is the OPCODE itself + the GameMessage header src (target actor) + the cached StatusBase pointer derived from the actor registry. For 0x017B: wire body is all-zero (8 bytes); FUN_006DBE50 writes target+0x5d = 0 always, then if the previous value was non-zero calls vtable[31] on the target - effectively a 'clear shadow flag' triggered by the opcode/header pairing. **Catalog updates**: 5 new entries in data_dependency_catalog.json receiverWriteIndex (CharaBase.0x60.0x00, CharaBase.0x60.0x58, CharaBase.0x60.0x59 for 0x013D; CharaBase.0xDC.0x18 for 0x0144; CharaBase.0xDC.0x10 for 0x0145). receiverWritesIndexed total: 18 -> 23. Confidence on the 0x0144/0x0145 entries is 'medium' because Ghidra didn't fully infer the ECX-passed 'this' at the FUN_006EEC00 callsites; the structural pattern (lazy 0x1C-byte sub-struct at +0xDC) is solid but callsite-level verification would require dynamic trace or manual assembly inspection. **Receivers-with-actor-writes count update**: pre-16a was 19/38 (per the receiver-classification pass); 4 of the 7 the inbound-payload-schemas pass receivers were already counted (0x017B via BCS-Y-0278, 0x013D was a 'set' but its actual write offsets are NEW here, 0x0144/0x0145 are NEW). The receiver-apply-findings pass adds 3 receivers to the with-writes set: 0x013D, 0x0144, 0x0145. New count: 19 -> 22/38. (0x0136/0x0137/0x0179 still indirect and not yet directly mapped to actor fields; 0x017B was already counted.) **Open questions**: (1) FUN_006EEC00's ECX-passed 'this' at the FUN_006EECB0 / FUN_006FA980 callsites isn't Ghidra-inferred; the pattern strongly suggests target actor but needs callsite-level confirmation. (2) FUN_00707D60 (called by 0x0179's slot-3 dispatcher) was not decomped - exact field write offset for 0x0179 status update remains unknown. (3) `_onUpdateDisplayName` was previously excluded from the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass bridge as a false positive; the receiver-apply-findings pass evidence shows it's a CORRECT direct binding for 0x013D (depth-2 fire in the apply chain). A future the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass bridge update could re-admit it plus `_onChangeNetStatUser`/`_onChangeNetStatSystem` as new direct bindings for 0x013D / 0x0145 / 0x0145. symbols.name: bridge_apply_chain_firers_admit_3
symbols.notes:
**the apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass: the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass bridge update with 3 apply-chain Lua firers from the receiver-apply-findings pass**. The receiver-apply-findings pass (BCS-Y-0349) decomped 7 inbound receiver apply chains and surfaced 3 Lua firers from depth-2 apply helpers, NOT from LuaActorImpl::vftable slot dispatchers: _onUpdateDisplayName fires from FUN_006FAFF0 (SetDisplayNameReceiver / 0x013D); _onChangeNetStatUser and _onChangeNetStatSystem both fire from FUN_006FA980 (ChangeActorExtraStatReceiver / 0x0145, respectively via bit-diff loops at bits 8..15 and 0x10..0x12).

**Two changes to build_lua_to_opcode.py**:
1. Tightened source filter to exclude refs whose symbol name contains '_paired' or '_secondary'. BCS-Y-0238's symbol `LuaActorImpl::vftable_slot63_onUpdateDisplayName_paired_FUN_00759FD0` was admitting _onUpdateDisplayName to slot 63 as a name-luaactorimpl ref, which bound it to SendLogReceiver's 20-opcode range 0x0157..0x016A as false positives. The '_paired' suffix is BCS-Y-0238's explicit signal that this slot mirrors slot 62 by name only; the slot 63 dispatcher is actually SendLog (PURE-NATIVE, fires no Lua callback).

Reads manifests/lua_apply_chain_firers.json (generated by tools/extractors/build_apply_chain_firers.py from receiver_apply_findings_wire_derived.json) and merges firers as opcode bindings with mechanism='apply_chain'. They count toward luaNamesWithOpcode because they're still direct wire bindings (the opcode causes the Lua-callback to fire), but carry a distinct mechanism flag so consumers can distinguish from LuaActorImpl-slot bindings.

**Bridge state delta** (lua_to_opcode.json after rebuild):
- luaNamesWithOpcode: 11 -> 13 (+2 net: _onChangeNetStatUser, _onChangeNetStatSystem; _onUpdateDisplayName was already slot-bound to 0x013D via BCS-Y-0160)
- luaNamesWithSlotBasedBinding: 11 (unchanged; the 11 slot-based bindings remain)
- luaNamesWithApplyChainBinding: 0 -> 3 (NEW)
- luaNamesWithIndirectBinding: 6 (unchanged)
- Total bridged: 17 -> 19 (+2 net new Lua-names)
- inboundOpcodesWithLuaName: 31 -> 11 (false-positive removal for SendLog range 0x0157..0x016A; these 20 opcodes are now correctly back in inboundOpcodesGap as PURE-NATIVE)

symbols.name: substruct_cross_ref_4_new_indirect_bindings
symbols.notes:
**the apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass: N-API cross-ref re-run against the receiver-apply-findings pass sub-struct writes**. The lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass cross-ref pipeline (build_data_dependency_catalog.py) keys writes by (actorClass, flat offset). The receiver-apply-findings pass added 5 chain-keyed write entries to receiverWriteIndex (CharaBase.0x60.{0x00,0x58,0x59} for 0x013D SetDisplayName; CharaBase.0xDC.{0x10,0x18} for 0x0145 ChangeActorExtraStat / 0x0144 ChangeActorSubStatModeBorder) that the flat-offset cross-ref cannot match against N-API readers. This adds three sub-struct-aware match mechanisms:

1. **nested_match** (highest confidence): N-API's `nestedReads[]` entry `{outer, inner}` directly mirrors a writer chain key `Class.outer.inner`. Exact byte-level field overlap.
2. **substruct_accessor_semantic**: N-API calls FUN_006EEC00 (the CharaBase+0xDC sub-struct lazy accessor) in its chasedCallees AND the N-API's Lua-name semantically mirrors the apply-chain firer naming (the receiver-apply-findings pass evidence). High confidence when bit-range semantic matches.
3. **substruct_pointer_structural**: N-API reads the outer sub-struct pointer directly (e.g. CharaBase+0x60) without further chase recorded. The reader and writer share the same sub-struct; high confidence at the sub-struct-record level.

**4 new confirmed indirect bindings**:
- `_getDisplayName <- 0x013D` (nested_match: N-API impl 0x006FA4C0 has nestedRead {outer: 0x60, inner: 0x58} which exactly mirrors SetDisplayNameReceiver's write at CharaBase.0x60.0x58 - the display name kind selector field).
- `_getLocalizedDisplayName <- 0x013D` (substruct_pointer_structural: N-API impl 0x006FA3D0 reads CharaBase+0x60 directly; SetDisplayNameReceiver writes the displayName sub-struct at +0x60).
- `_getNetStatUser <- 0x0145` (substruct_accessor_semantic: N-API impl 0x006FA250 calls FUN_006EEC00 in chasedCallees + the receiver-apply-findings pass's _onChangeNetStatUser fire site evidence for ChangeActorExtraStatReceiver's u32 write at CharaBase.0xDC.0x10 bits 8..15).
- `_getNetStatSystem <- 0x0145` (substruct_accessor_semantic: mirror of _getNetStatUser; FUN_006EEC00 in chasedCallees + the receiver-apply-findings pass's _onChangeNetStatSystem fire site for bits 0x10..0x12 of the same u32).

**Bridge state delta** (lua_to_opcode.json after rebuild):
- luaNamesWithIndirectBinding: 6 -> 10 (+4 new)
- Total bridged Lua-names: 19 -> 23 (13 direct + 10 indirect)
- inboundOpcodesIndirectlyResolved: 4 (unchanged; 0x013D and 0x0145 are both already directly bound, so the new indirect readers don't extend the OPCODE coverage axis - they extend the LUA-NAME coverage axis)

**Total confirmedIndirectBindings**: 6 -> 10. data_dependency_catalog.json gains a `crossRef` audit-trail section recording the new bindings.

**Bridge schema enhancement**: build_lua_to_opcode.py's indirect-binding merge now preserves the mechanism field from the catalog (was hardcoded 'data_dependency'). Each indirect binding now carries its specific mechanism flag (nested_match vs substruct_accessor_semantic vs substruct_pointer_structural vs data_dependency).

**Why the +0xDC sub-struct case needs special handling**: 1.x's CharaBase has a 0x1C-byte lazily-allocated sub-struct at offset 0xDC accessed via FUN_006EEC00 (the receiver-apply-findings pass). N-API readers like _getNetStatUser do `param_1 + 0x10` (a SEPARATE work-block pointer) then call FUN_006EEC00 (which returns the +0xDC sub-struct) to read the net-stat data. The recursive field-access extractor sees the +0x10 read but doesn't chase through FUN_006EEC00 to discover the +0xDC.0x10 access. The apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass's substruct_accessor_semantic rule patches this gap by recognizing the FUN_006EEC00 callsite signature.

**Tooling**: tools/extractors/build_substruct_cross_ref.py runs the cross-ref. Outputs: appends 4 entries to manifests/data_dependency_catalog.json confirmedIndirectBindings + new crossRef section, then bridge rebuild via tools/build_lua_to_opcode.py.

symbols.name: FUN_006EEC00_ECX_this_verified
symbols.notes:
**the apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass: FUN_006EEC00 ECX 'this' verification - closes last the receiver-apply-findings pass open question**. The receiver-apply-findings pass left the 0x0144 and 0x0145 field-write claims at medium confidence because Ghidra's decompiler did not infer the ECX-passed 'this' pointer at the FUN_006EECB0 / FUN_006FA980 callsites to FUN_006EEC00 (the lazy CharaBase+0xDC sub-struct accessor). The apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass does the manual assembly trace via a new Ghidra script DumpFunctionListing.java.

**Verification chain for 0x0144** (FUN_008A32C0 Receive -> FUN_006EECB0 helper -> FUN_006EEC00):

FUN_008A32C0 (Receive, 46 bytes): RTTI cast at 0x008a32d6 (CALL 0x009DA6CC) converts ActorBase to CharaBase, returning the CharaBase ptr in EAX. Then `MOV ECX, EAX` at 0x008a32e3 sets up the call with ECX = CharaBase, and CALL 0x006EECB0 at 0x008a32e5 dispatches.

FUN_006EECB0 (helper, 26 bytes): `MOV ESI, ECX` at 0x006eecb1 preserves CharaBase 'this' in ESI. Two consecutive CALL 0x006EEC00 invocations follow; between them, `MOV ECX, ESI` at 0x006eecb8 restores ECX from the saved CharaBase ptr (because FUN_006EEC00 trashes ECX as a callee-clobbered reg). Both calls pass `this = CharaBase` to FUN_006EEC00. After the second call returns EAX = sub-struct ptr (CharaBase+0xDC), `MOV [EAX + 0x18], CL` at 0x006eecc3 writes the mode byte at sub_struct+0x18.

**Verification chain for 0x0145** (FUN_0089C990 Receive -> FUN_006FA980 helper -> FUN_006EEC00):

FUN_0089C990 (Receive, 52 bytes): Same RTTI cast pattern; `MOV ECX, EAX` at 0x0089c9b9 sets ECX = CharaBase before CALL 0x006FA980 at 0x0089c9bb.

FUN_006FA980 (helper, 1255 bytes): `MOV EDI, ECX` at 0x006fa9ad preserves CharaBase 'this' in EDI. First CALL 0x006EEC00 at 0x006fa9af passes ECX = CharaBase. After the call, `MOV ECX, EDI` at 0x006fa9ca restores ECX for the second CALL 0x006EEC00 at 0x006fa9cc. The write at 0x006fa9da is `MOV [EAX + 0x10], ESI` (new u32 net-stat flags at sub_struct+0x10).

**FUN_006EEC00 internals** (149 bytes): Prologue does `MOV EDI, ECX` at 0x006eec24, then `MOV EAX, [EDI + 0xdc]` at 0x006eec26 - directly uses ECX as 'this' to read the +0xdc sub-struct pointer. Confirms thiscall convention with ECX = target actor.

**Confidence upgrades**:
- CharaBase.0xDC.0x18 write (0x0144 sub-stat mode border): medium -> high
- CharaBase.0xDC.0x10 write (0x0145 net-stat flags u32): medium -> high

Updated both receiver_apply_findings_wire_derived.json's actorWrites entries (with asm-grounded evidence pointers) and data_dependency_catalog.json's chain-key entries (`confidenceUpgradedBy` field cites this BCS-Y).

**The receiver-apply-findings pass openQuestions[] now empty** (3 -> 0). All three open questions resolved: _onUpdateDisplayName re-admit (the apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass), FUN_00707D60 decomp (the apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass), FUN_006EEC00 ECX verification (the apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass here). Added a `closedQuestions` list summarizing the resolution chain and a `closure` section with the asm-trace evidence pointer.

symbols.name: remaining_9_receivers_structural_classification
symbols.notes:
**the receiver-apply-findings pass: apply-decomp on the 9 remaining wire-confirmed inbound receivers**. The lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass wire-confirmed 16/38 inbound receivers via pcap; the receiver-apply-findings pass + 18b covered the 7 heaviest (30..79 sample counts) plus 0x0179's depth-4 worker. The receiver-apply-findings pass extends to the remaining 9 receivers (2..38 sample counts) via Ghidra batch decomp (DumpFunctionDecomp + DumpVtableSlots) of slot1Fn + apply helpers + queue/factory helpers + secondary vftable slots.

**Receivers covered**: 0x00D3 SetTargetTime, 0x012E SetTalkEventCondition, 0x0131 EndClientOrderEvent, 0x0133 UserDataReceiver, 0x0157..0x016A SendLog, 0x016B SetNoticeEventCondition, 0x016F SetPushEventConditionWithCircle, 0x0195 HateStatus.

**Structural classification** (4 categories surfaced):

(1) **Apply-chain Lua fire only** [0x00D3 SetTargetTime]: 2-slot receiver; slot1Fn FUN_008A04B0 (400B) does time arithmetic via FUN_0075BDA0 (get-current-time). Two branches: (A) FUN_008A0700 (123B) instantiates a Timer object for future expiration (param_4/param_5 stored at +0xe/+0xf); (B) FUN_008A0370 (317B) fires _onReceiveTimingPacket Lua callback on the expired/zero-time path via the canonical FUN_00447260 + FUN_00CC7A90 pattern. Already slot-61 bound in the bridge; the receiver-apply-findings pass adds DUAL EVIDENCE apply-chain binding alongside the existing slot binding.

(2) **Event-condition deferred-apply** [0x012E, 0x016B, 0x016F, 0x0131]: True 2-slot Receivers (slot1Fn IS the Receive entry) that construct event-condition objects rather than mutating actor state directly. The Receive entries do ActorBase->NpcBase/DirectorBase RTTI casts and dispatch to object-constructor helpers: SetNotice -> FUN_006F1380 / FUN_006F2E80 build NoticeBlock or NoticeNonBlock via FUN_00892770/FUN_008927F0; SetTalk -> FUN_006F29B0 builds TalkBlock/TalkNonBlock via FUN_00892D00/FUN_00892E30; SetPushCircle -> FUN_006F2B70 -> FUN_006F2310 build push-block; EndClientOrder -> FUN_0089D070 sets its own vftable + copies 3 bytes from receiver. The constructed event-condition objects are queued for deferred processing elsewhere; nothing in these apply chains writes to actor state directly.

(3) **Buffer-copy** [0x0133 UserData]: 6-slot Receiver. slot1Fn FUN_008A2A20 is a tiny 16-byte getter that calls slot 5 factory FUN_0089F070 (allocates 0x24-byte object via malloc, sets UserDataReceiver::vftable + CommandInterface::vftable, calls FUN_0089EFA0 which memcpys wire payload bytes into a buffer at obj+0x14). The Lua side reads this buffer via _onReceiveDataPacket (existing slot-59 binding). No direct actor-state writes.

(4) **Already documented** [0x0195 HateStatus, SendLog 0x0157..0x016A]: HateStatusReceiver writes NpcBase+0x154 (u32 enmity amount) + NpcBase+0x158 (u16 enmity kind) per BCS-Y-0278; the receiver-apply-findings pass re-decomp serves as cross-confirmation. SendLogReceiver is a 1092-byte log-record builder switching on log kind byte; PURE-NATIVE per BCS-Y-0238.

**Bridge state delta**:
- NEW apply-chain firer: _onReceiveTimingPacket <- 0x00D3 (DUAL evidence with existing slot-61 binding; doesn't increase luaNamesWithOpcode but bumps luaNamesWithApplyChainBinding 4 -> 5).
- NO new chain-key writes in receiverWriteIndex. The 9 the receiver-apply-findings pass receivers overwhelmingly use deferred patterns; actor-state writes happen in CONSUMER code that processes queued event-objects, not in the Receive apply chain.

**Vftable layouts captured** (receiver_apply_findings_remaining.json::vtableLayouts): SetNoticeEventCondition, SetTalkEventCondition, SetPushEventConditionWithCircle, EndClientOrderEvent, UserDataReceiver. Notable: SetNotice and SetPush vftables overlap at offset +0xC (multi-inheritance secondary vftable; the same function FUN_0089DB00 appears at SetNotice slot 4 AND SetPush slot 1).

**Tooling**:
- tools/extractors/build_apply_chain_firers.py extended to read both receiver_apply_findings_wire_derived.json AND receiver_apply_findings_remaining.json (FINDINGS_SOURCES list, deduplicates on (luaName, opcode)).
- Sibling-repo xivl-opcodes/tools/extractors/inject_apply_chain_readers.py re-run to absorb the new apply-chain reader for SetTargetTimeReceiver.
- 4 Ghidra decomp dumps: receives_decomp.txt (8 slot1Fn entries), helpers_decomp.txt (8 apply helpers), deeper_decomp.txt (6 queue/state-machine helpers), vtable_slots.txt (30 vftable slot lookups across 5 5/6-slot receivers).

**Structural insight**: the 7 receivers the receiver-apply-findings pass covered are precisely the ones that do 'apply-now, fire-callback-now' with direct CharaBase/PlayerBase/NpcBase writes. The 9 the receiver-apply-findings pass receivers are precisely the ones that buffer/queue/defer. This split correlates with pcap sample frequency: high-traffic receivers (>= 30 samples) update real-time per-actor state, while lower-traffic receivers (2..38 samples) configure deferred event conditions. The apply-chain-and-substruct-evidence pass sub-struct cross-ref and the receiver-apply-findings pass's direct write extraction have effectively saturated the receiver-side write evidence available from the wire-confirmed receivers.

symbols.name: event_condition_consumer_tracing
symbols.notes:
**the event-condition-consumer-findings pass: event-condition consumer tracing**. The receiver-apply-findings pass classified opcodes 0x012E/0x016B/0x016F/0x0131 as deferred-apply receivers that construct queued event-condition objects rather than mutating actor state directly. The event-condition-consumer-findings pass follows those constructed objects through their vftables to identify Lua-name firers in the consumer (queue-drain) chain.

**Event-condition vftables identified** (named by Ghidra symbol table via `*param_1 = Application::Lua::Script::Client::Event::<class>::vftable` constructor patterns):
- NoticeBlock @ 0x01056E0C (ctor FUN_00892770)
- NoticeNonBlock @ 0x01056E40 (ctor FUN_008927F0)
- TalkBlock @ 0x01056F44 (ctor FUN_00892D00)
- TalkNonBlock @ 0x01056F78 (ctor FUN_00892E30)
- PushBlock @ 0x01056EDC (ctor FUN_00892980)
- PushNonBlock @ 0x01056F10 (ctor FUN_00892B40)

All 6 share a 12-slot layout (0x00..0x2C, RTTI at 0x30). Shared base virtuals across all 6 classes:
- Slot 0x04 (FUN_00897570): sets up Lua args, dispatches via `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x28))(...)` to per-class execute.
- Slot 0x08 (FUN_00712B40): empty noop.
- Slot 0x0C (FUN_00897660): FIRES `_onPreEvent` via FUN_00447260 + FUN_00CC7A90.
- Slot 0x10 (FUN_008977B0): FIRES `_onPostEvent` via same.

Per-family slot 0x14/0x18: kind getter + matcher returning ASCII char constants (Notice 0x012c3f7e, Talk 0x012c3f7a, Push 0x012c3f7b). Slot 0x1C: Block returns 1, NonBlock returns 0.

**Per-class slot 0x28 execute virtuals** (dispatched by slot 0x04):
- TalkBlock FUN_00892D70 fires `_onTalkEvent`
- TalkNonBlock FUN_00892E90 fires `_onTalkRequest`
- PushBlock FUN_00892A80 fires `_onPushEvent`
- PushNonBlock FUN_00892C30 fires `_onPushRequest`
- NoticeBlock FUN_008927E0: empty noop (no family-specific Lua fire; only base _onPreEvent/_onPostEvent for Notice).
- NoticeNonBlock FUN_00892850: empty noop.

**Bridge state delta** (lua_to_opcode.json):
- 10 NEW (luaName, opcode) bindings; 6 distinct Lua names bridged for the first time:
 - `_onPreEvent` <- 0x012E + 0x016B + 0x016F (via 6-class shared base slot 0x0C)
 - `_onPostEvent` <- 0x012E + 0x016B + 0x016F (via 6-class shared base slot 0x10)
 - `_onTalkEvent` <- 0x012E (via TalkBlock slot 0x28)
 - `_onTalkRequest` <- 0x012E (via TalkNonBlock slot 0x28)
 - `_onPushEvent` <- 0x016F (via PushBlock slot 0x28)
 - `_onPushRequest` <- 0x016F (via PushNonBlock slot 0x28)
- luaNamesWithOpcode: 14 -> 20 (+6)
- luaNamesWithApplyChainBinding: 5 -> 11 (+6)
- NEW count: luaNamesWithDeferredApplyChainBinding = 6 (all 6 new firers tagged bindingFlavor='deferred_via_event_condition')

- New manifest: manifests/event_condition_consumer_findings.json (consumed by build_apply_chain_firers.py via FINDINGS_SOURCES list).
- build_apply_chain_firers.py: added event_condition_consumer_findings.json source, propagates new `bindingFlavor` field per firer (default 'direct'; event_condition_consumer_findings.json entries use 'deferred_via_event_condition').

- xivl-opcodes/tools/extractors/inject_apply_chain_readers.py: also propagates bindingFlavor into client_receivers.json apply_chain_lua_readers entries.

**0x0131 EndClientOrderEvent** (structurally different pattern - documented but yields no new bridge bindings):
- 5-slot Receiver vtable at 0x01057348; slot1Fn FUN_0089D180 queues a NEW EndClientOrderEventReceiver instance (not a separate Block/NonBlock class) constructed by FUN_0089D070.
- Consumer dispatch: slot 0x0C (FUN_0089E2D0) -> FUN_008A13A0 switch on byte at *param_1. Cases 0..5 load `*(param_2+0x18)` and sub-switch to FUN_006E1080/A0/C0/E0 thin wrappers which call FUN_008934A0/3520/35B0/3800. Cases 0x32..0x37 dispatch via FUN_008A10C0 sub-switch to FUN_006E1100/1120.

The 3 newly-bridged opcodes (0x012E/0x016B/0x016F) had zero direct or indirect bindings before the event-condition-consumer-findings pass, so deferred firers are the only available evidence path. 0x0131 EndClientOrderEvent uses a self-class-queue pattern that touches only sub-object state flags and remains unbridged.

symbols.name: WS_H_deferred_lua_napi_mutator_catalog
symbols.notes:
**the ws-b-substruct-accessor-sweep pass / WS-H: deferred-Lua N-API mutator catalog import**.

**Motivation**: the deferred-napi-writers pass (BCS-Y-0358) traced opcodes 0x012E/0x016B/0x016F through their event-condition consumer chains into 6 N-API mutator methods on PlayerBase/MyPlayer that target global subsystem state via the FUN_004D7580 singleton. The deferred-napi-writers pass explicitly did not write these into data_dependency_catalog.json because the chain-key indirect-binding schema (which pairs N-API readers with per-actor field writes) doesn't model deferred Lua-to-N-API mutator chains. WS-H closes that gap by adding a parallel binding category.

**Schema extension**: New top-level key `deferredLuaNapiMutatorBindings` in data_dependency_catalog.json. Each binding is (luaEventName, luaEventClass) keyed and records: writingOpcodes (opcodes whose event-condition receivers ultimately fire the handler), writingReceivers (receiver name + applyVa + bcsyRef per opcode), napiMutators (mutator name + full stub/vtable/override/wrapper/singleton-slot chain for the 6 PlayerBase lock methods, lighter metadata for RPC/generic-dispatch mutators), uiSideMutators (desktopWidget calls), subsystemStateTouched, guard (when present), and full 10-level call-chain evidence string. fireChainBcsy = BCS-Y-0356 (the event-condition-consumer-findings pass/b apply-chain firers); tracingBcsy = BCS-Y-0358 (the deferred-napi-writers pass trace).

**6 bindings imported**: (1) PlayerBaseClass::_onPreEvent fires from 0x012E/0x016B/0x016F, calls _unlockPlayerControl + _unlockLockonControl, clears PlayerControl/LockonControl/TargetCursorControl lock counters on event entry. (2) PlayerBaseClass::_onPostEvent (guarded by commandJudgeMode/commandContent) fires from same 3 opcodes, calls _lockPlayerControl + _lockLockonControl, sets lock counters on event exit when in command mode. (3) NpcBaseClass::_onTalkEvent fires from 0x012E, calls _doServerOnTalk (server-RPC, not local mutator). (4) NpcBaseClass::_onTalkRequest fires from 0x012E, calls _callServerOnEmote (server-RPC). (5) NpcBaseClass::_onPushEvent fires from 0x016F (guarded by pushCommandIn), calls setPlaceDrivenCommandVariation on PlaceDriven subsystem. (6) NpcBaseClass::_onPushRequest fires from 0x016F, calls _callFunction (generic delegated dispatch, target varies).

**No bridge-count delta**: the lua_to_opcode bridge tracks (luaName, opcode) bindings; these 6 entries are catalog-side evidence for the same 6 deferred apply-chain bindings already captured by `bindingFlavor: deferred_via_event_condition` in the event-condition-consumer-findings pass/b. lua_to_opcode counts unchanged: luaNamesWithOpcode=20, luaNamesWithApplyChainBinding=11 (5 direct + 6 deferred), luaNamesWithDeferredApplyChainBinding=6, inboundOpcodesWithLuaName=15.

**Resolves the original /loop condition**: the receiver-apply-findings pass follow-on predicted '2-4 new chain-key writes' from event-condition consumer tracing. The event-condition-consumer-findings pass proved that prediction structurally false in C++ (no synchronous chain-key writes exist on this path). The deferred-napi-writers pass found that the actual mutations happen via N-API mutators called from Lua handlers, targeting global subsystem state. WS-H lands 6 catalog entries documenting those mutator bindings in a new schema category that respects the empirical mutation shape.

symbols.name: pcap_empirical_validation_of_bridge_opcodes
symbols.notes:
**the pcap-validation pass: PCAP empirical validation of bridge opcodes**. Scanned the 54-capture 1.x pcap corpus at `xivl-captures/captures` to verify whether the 14 distinct inbound opcodes referenced by the 23 confirmed indirect bridge bindings are actually observed in real server-to-client traffic. **Methodology**; TCP-reassembled BasePacket/SubPacket parser; SubPacket.cs). BasePacket compressed bodies (s2c is mostly zlib-compressed) decompressed via zlib (with raw-deflate fallback). SubPacket type 0x03 = game-message wrapper containing the opcode. Direction tagged by client IP 192.168.1.101 (server is 202.67.51.120 in the canonical captures). Implemented in `tools/validate_pcap_bridge.py`. **Critical parser detail**: initial implementation used a strict bail-on-bad-header policy, which only found 7 distinct s2c opcodes (under-count by 14x). Switching to resync-on-bad-header (advance 1 byte and retry) surfaced 100 distinct s2c opcodes and 23 distinct c2s opcodes. The bail policy was wrong because TCP reassembly across streams produces concat-friendly bytes but not always BasePacket-aligned starts; resync is required to skip stream-prefix handshake bytes. **Results - 10 of 14 bridge opcodes observed in s2c traffic**:
- 0x013d: 235 hits across 13/54 captures (combat_autoattack, gridania, etc)
- 0x0144: 265 hits across 23/54 captures (action_and_traits, change_helm, etc)
- 0x0145: 236 hits across 13/54 captures
- 0x0179: 236 hits across 13/54 captures
- 0x0194: 9 hits across 9/54 captures (mostly transition/login)
- 0x0195: 37 hits across 3/54 captures (combat_autoattack, combat_skills, party)
- 0x0197: 1 hit in gridania_to_coerthas.pcapng (chocobo grade change)
- 0x019c: 9 hits across 9/54 captures (achievement points)
- 0x019d: 9 hits across 9/54 captures (achievement title)
- 0x01a4: 10 hits across 10/54 captures (job change) **Results - 4 bridge opcodes NOT observed in s2c traffic**:
- 0x018e ChangeSystemStat: capture corpus lacks the system-stat events that fire this. Plausible interpretation: ChangeSystemStat fires on login/zone-transition system state recovery, which our captures didn't exercise in observable form. - 0x01a1: opcode binding via _onChangeJob path; captures don't include the specific subevent that emits 0x01a1 (vs the observed 0x01a4). - 0x01a6 HamletSupplyRanking: content-gated (1.x Hamlet defense), not present in the captured gameplay sessions. - 0x01a8 HamletDefenseScore: same content gate as 0x01a6. **Validation rate**: 10/14 = 71% of bridge opcodes have empirical packet evidence in the available corpus. The 4 misses are explainable by content gating, not by binding error. Confidence in the bridge increases from 'static decomp claim' to 'static decomp claim + observed packet evidence' for 71% of indexed opcodes. **Secondary finding**: the corpus surfaces 100 distinct s2c opcodes vs only 55 in the inbound receiver map. The gap of 45 opcodes is fresh evidence territory - opcodes that appear in real packets but are not yet receiver-mapped in the catalog. This is a new bridge-extension vector: empirical opcode discovery from PCAP, distinct from the static-decomp-driven receiver mapping methodology. **Bridge metrics**: unchanged (no new chain keys, no new bindings; this manifest grounds existing bindings rather than adding new ones).

symbols.name: bridge_project_milestone_close
symbols.notes:
**BRIDGE PROJECT CLOSE: load-bearing milestone summary**.

This entry is the project-level epitaph for the Lua N-API <-> wire opcode bridge workstream. It records the final state, the methodologies tried, the architectural ceilings discovered, and the concrete resumption points. The earlier per-phase BCS-Y entries (BCS-Y-0327 onward for s2c the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass+, BCS-Y-0375 onward for c2s the bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass+) carry implementation detail; this entry exists so a future agent can orient on a single reference instead of reconstructing the trajectory from 60+ phase entries.

**Final binding counts:**
- s2c confirmedIndirectBindings: 23 across 10 distinct opcodes; 71% PCAP-validated; methodology terminal.
- c2s outboundOpcodeBindings: 11 across 6 distinct opcodes (8 direct_emit + 2 state_trigger + 1 catalog-gap-recovered); methodology saturated.
- Combined: 34 confirmed bridge bindings across 16 distinct opcodes.
- BCS-Y catalog: 387 entries at close (this entry included).

**s2c arc (the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass..30):**
- the lua-name-to-opcode-bridge-open pass..19 established the receiver -> actor field -> Lua N-API model. Receivers are dispatched through FUN_004DC690 (central packet router) and FUN_004D8860 (event-family router), with 2-slot / 5-slot / 6-slot vtable layouts (slot[1] is the New() factory for 5/6-slot, not Receive).
- the event-condition-consumer-findings pass..23 enumerated the 15 Control-class N-API switchboards (CharaBase, PlayerBase, NpcBase, DirectorBase, AreaBase, PrivateAreaBase, GroupBase, ItemBase, ActorBase, WidgetBase, WorldMaster, Debug, DesktopWidget, Global, SpreadSheet) covering 364 N-APIs total.
- the event-condition-tracing-and-rigorous-negatives pass introduced the flat_chain_key cross-ref mechanism: receiverWriteIndex {opcode, targetClass, offset} matched against N-API recursiveReads/recursiveNestedReads. This produced most of the 23 bindings.
- the pcap-validation pass PCAP-validated the bridge: 10 of 14 indexed bridge opcodes observed in real packets (71%). Critical parser detail: resync-on-bad-header is required; strict-bail under-counts s2c traffic by 14x. Secondary finding: 100 distinct s2c opcodes in pcaps vs 55 in the receiver mapping.
- the bridge-project-close pass explored the gap. **Architectural conclusion: the remaining s2c opcodes do not use the Receiver-class pattern.** Actual observed-minus-mapped set is 68 opcodes (not 45 -- the delta was a count, not a set diff). The receiver-discovery pass probed the top 10 by pcap count and classified the non-matches into three patterns:
 - direct_non_receiver_handler: dispatcher routes to inline C++ functions; state updates are local/container/UI, not canonical actor offsets. Examples: 0x0190 (1621 hits), 0x018d, 0x0146.
 - group_sharedwork_non_receiver: routes through Group::PacketProcessor / SharedWork. The bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass already proved this path has no safe GroupBase write chain. Examples: 0x017c, 0x017d, 0x017e, 0x0183.
 - no_case_in_documented_routers: a third dispatch mechanism exists but is unmapped. Examples: 0x0134, 0x0139, 0x0147.

**c2s arc (the bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass..29f):**
- the bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass (BCS-Y-0375): first c2s binding, CharaBase._setPosition -> 0x00ca via scene-record state trigger through FUN_0075F120 -> FUN_004D7980(0x24/0x25). Chain documented end-to-end including the three known 0x00ca emitters (FUN_004DC690 case 7, FUN_00589030 dirty-bit flush, FUN_0058E0C0 case 0x51) and packet builder FUN_004DD620.
- the scene-record-choke-point pass (BCS-Y-0376): generalized the choke-point methodology around FUN_004D7980. 246 callers, 190 unique, but only 2 Lua APIs reach the choke point at BFS depth 3. Added _setDirection as the second state-trigger binding. Calibration finding: ~0.5% Lua-impl coverage per choke point.
- the scene-record-depth-bfs pass (BCS-Y-0377): tested depth as the constraint. Depths 3/5/7 all yielded the same 8 reachable APIs. Depth was not the bottleneck.
- the record-id-emitter-trace pass (BCS-Y-0378): traced the 6 unverified scene-state posters. All 6 had record IDs (0x00, 0x12, 0x26, 0x32, 0x33) outside the known 0x00ca emitter switch tables. Choke-point methodology exhausted.
- the sibling-choke-points pass (BCS-Y-0379): discovered 26 sibling choke points via FUN_004EC080 callers. Only 1 was Lua-reachable (_setVisible -> FUN_004D7890) and it stayed local. The scene-record system is overwhelmingly C++-internal, not a Lua-driven emission gateway.
- the direct-emission pass (BCS-Y-0380): pivoted to forward direct-emission mining. 1 binding found at BFS depth 5: CharaBase._updateGroup -> 0x0130 (direct emit, stack packet via FUN_0075E860). New binding kind confirmed_direct_emit introduced.
- the depth-extended-direct-emission pass (BCS-Y-0381): tested depth on direct-emission. Depths 5/8/10 all yielded the same 1 binding. Forward direction depth-saturated.
- **the reverse-bfs-send-helpers pass (BCS-Y-0382) was the methodological breakthrough**: reverse-BFS from send helpers (FUN_004D6D10, FUN_004D6D30, FUN_004E0240, FUN_00DAE010, FUN_004DD620, FUN_0075E860). 53 packet builders identified, 7 new bindings (3.3x jump). Reverse-BFS dramatically outperformed forward because vtable indirection breaks forward traversal but every send-helper CALL is a literal machine-code instruction with a static caller list. New opcode coverage: 0x00cc, 0x00cd, 0x0131; existing 0x0130 family expanded.
- the bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass (BCS-Y-0383): recovered the 0x0132 catalog gap. ItemBase._updateWork -> 0x0132 was a Lua-reachable binding rejected only because 0x0132 was absent from operation_opcode_map_outbound.json. Adding the catalog entry as tentative ItemWorkUpdatePacket promoted the binding.
- the expanded-reverse-bfs pass (BCS-Y-0384): expanded reverse-BFS to 56 entry points. 0 new bindings, 2 new catalog-gap candidates surfaced (0x00d0 size 0x110 via 0x00763DC0; 0x0134 size 0x28 via 0x0075EBA0; both with no Lua reach in the current scan). Reverse-BFS saturated.

**Methodology calibration matrix:**
- s2c Receiver-class + cross-ref: WORKED (23 bindings, terminal at the architectural ceiling).
- s2c direct_non_receiver / Group/SharedWork / third-router: UNEXPLORED in depth, but the bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass + the receiver-discovery pass strongly suggest low EV.
- c2s choke-point BFS depth (29a + 29d): NULL across all tested depths.
- c2s sibling choke-points (29b + 29b1): 1 candidate, 0 bindings (scene-record system is C++-internal).
- c2s forward direct-emission (29c): 1 binding at depth 5; depth-extended (29d) null.
- c2s reverse-BFS (29e): 7 bindings, the breakthrough method.
- c2s expanded reverse-BFS (29f): saturated; no second-tier packet builders found.

**Why the project stops here:**
The 34-binding state is bounded by *architectural* findings, not by methodology gaps:
- s2c: the 23 confirmed bindings cover every Receiver-class opcode whose receiver writes a canonical actor offset that any N-API reads. The remaining s2c opcodes (45+ observed in pcaps but not bound) use dispatch patterns that do not write canonical actor offsets in any binding-friendly way -- proven for Group/SharedWork (the bridge-growth-and-ceiling pass) and demonstrated for direct handlers (the receiver-discovery pass).
- c2s: the 11 confirmed bindings cover every Lua N-API that reaches a known send helper through statically resolvable edges, plus the two state-trigger paths that the scene-record system exposes. Reverse-BFS at 56 entry points produced 0 second-tier builders. Further expansion would require new entry points (unmapped packet builders surfaced as catalog gaps) or new dispatch patterns.

**Concrete resumption points if the project is revived (highest EV first):**

*s2c side:*
1. Investigate direct_non_receiver_handler pattern at higher resolution. 0x0190 has 1621 hits and routes via 0x00576CD0. The receiver-discovery pass's quick probe noted local/container/UI state without proving an actor-write chain. A focused decomp of the 0x0190 inline path might surface a binding if the inline handler writes through a sub-struct pointer that any N-API reads. Cost: 1-2 days.
2. Locate the third dispatcher that handles 0x0134, 0x0139, 0x0147. None appear in FUN_004DC690 or FUN_004D8860. There must be a third routing mechanism (a vtable dispatch, a per-channel handler, or a special-case fast path). Cost: 1 day for the search; unknown for the binding harvest if found.
3. Re-run the receiver-discovery pass on the remaining 29 receiver-family candidates. The 0/10 stop gate was about yield, not a permanent ban. If the resumption agent has fresh ideas about the dispatcher walk, the remaining 29 are worth a second pass. Cost: 2-3 days.

*c2s side:*
4. Add 0x00d0 and 0x0134 to the outbound catalog (1-2h). Same pattern as 0x0132 recovery. No immediate binding payoff (the expanded-reverse-bfs pass found no Lua reach), but catalog completeness has independent value, and a future non-Control-class scan might surface Lua reach.
5. Non-Control-class Lua API scan. All 384 N-APIs in the corpus came from the 15 Control switchboards. There are likely other Lua entry points (script callbacks, event handlers, UI hooks) outside the Control namespace. Cost: multi-day; speculative.
6. Operation-class emission decomp. ~25 remaining serverboundGap opcodes have not been chased to their emission sites. Each is a deterministic decomp target -- mechanical but slow. Cost: multi-day.

**Load-bearing references (read these first if you resume):**

- BCS-Y-0279 + BCS-Y-0280: the FUN_004DC690 + FUN_004D8860 dispatcher documentation.

symbols.name: c2s_payload_struct_decoding
symbols.notes:
**the c2s-payload-decoding pass: c2s packet payload decoding for Lua-bound opcodes**. Decoded the c2s-payload-decoding pass outbound packet builders for the six c2s opcode families in outboundOpcodeBindings: 0x00ca, 0x00cc, 0x00cd, 0x0130, 0x0131, and 0x0132.

**Builder corpus:** 8 distinct builders/producer functions were covered: FUN_004DD620, FUN_00561BB0, FUN_00562D30, FUN_0075EB30, FUN_0075E860, FUN_0075E8D0, FUN_0075EA50, and FUN_0075EAC0. This yields 6 decomp-backed payload structs and 22 application-payload fields.

**Offset calibration:** all decoded builders use the same client packet-record convention: record+0 is the opcode literal, record+4 is the body-size literal, and record+0x18 is the first server-consumed application payload byte.  -> FUN_00cd7670 (27-byte thin wrapper, shifts args)
